goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
goldens.reasoning: C1 describes the same problem: removing the float from .panel inside the non-flex .row in the server-rendered header.

goldens.comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
goldens.reasoning: C2 is about a missing -moz-box-align, not about -ms-align-items being an invalid prefix.

goldens.comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
goldens.reasoning: No candidate raises the 0-based value problem with box-ordinal-group.

candidates: The server-rendered header (_header.html.erb) places .panel inside a Bootstrap .row, but the PR removes float: right and replaces it with flex-only positioning (margin-left: auto + order). Because .row is not a flex container, the login panel will no longer right-align and may drop below the title for logged-out pages.

The new flexbox()/inline-flex() mixins emit display: -moz-box / display: -moz-inline-box, but align-items() does not emit -moz-box-align. This creates inconsistent cross-browser behavior: any case that falls back to the -moz box model won't get the intended alignment (e.g., badge bullet baseline alignment).
